hero.headline: Two men killed in early morning shooting in Port St. Lucie neighborhood
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie Police Department is investigating a double fatal shooting that occurred early Sunday morning in a residential neighborhood. Officers responded around 3:30 a.m. to the 1300 block of Southeast Rivergreen Circle after receiving multiple 911 calls reporting gunshots. When officers arrived, they found two adult men suffering from multiple gunshot wounds in the driveways of a residence. Both victims were taken to separate local hospitals, where they later died from their injuries. Police identified the victims as Carl Loubeau, 24, and Juliun Stokes, 22.

Preliminary investigation indicates some of the people involved had been socializing earlier in the evening before returning to a home on Southeast Rivergreen Circle. Police said a verbal altercation occurred outside the residence over a residential key and escalated into an exchange of gunfire between two of the individuals involved. Investigators believe the shooting was an isolated incident involving people who knew one another and said there is no ongoing threat to the public. All parties involved have either been detained or are cooperating with investigators, according to police.

Neighbor John Adams was working in his garage when he heard the gunfire. "I was just working on my bicycle and I heard gunshots. Maybe two, three and I stayed in the garage and then I heard a girl screaming," Adams told WPTV reporter Zitlali Solache. Adams described a massive emergency response to the scene. "Every police officer in Port St. Lucie was here, there was twenty squads, two ambulances, two firetrucks, a helicopter. It was just mayhem," he said. Adams also said a police officer told him they took a picture of 16 casings. "Just devastating, terrible. My heart goes out to them," Adams said. Another neighbor who did not want to be identified said she dialed 911 and stayed with one of the wounded men until help arrived.

The investigation remains active as detectives continue conducting interviews, processing evidence and reviewing available information. Police said additional details, including any potential criminal charges, will be released as the investigation progresses. Anyone with information who has not yet spoken with detectives is asked to contact the Port St. Lucie Police Department.

cards.headline: Snyder Drives in Five as St. Lucie Mets Hold Off Cardinals, 8-6
cards.teaser:
Trey Snyder delivered a career day at the plate Sunday as the St. Lucie Mets held off a late Palm Beach Cardinals rally for an 8-6 victory at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

Snyder
cards.body:
Trey Snyder delivered a career day at the plate Sunday as the St. Lucie Mets held off a late Palm Beach Cardinals rally for an 8-6 victory at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

Snyder went 4-for-5 with a home run, triple and five RBIs, helping St. Lucie win the three-game series two games to one.

After allowing the Cardinals to score first in each of the opening two games, the Mets took control with three runs in the first inning.

Randy Guzman opened the scoring with a 107 mph ground ball that Palm Beach third baseman Jonathan Mejia stopped but could not make a throw on, allowing Marco Vargas to score. Snyder followed with a two-run single that gave the Mets a 3-0 lead.

Starting pitcher Ethan Lanthier worked through early traffic and completed 2 1/3 scoreless innings. He allowed one hit and struck out four.

Tyler McLoughlin followed with 1 2/3 scoreless innings and earned the victory, improving his record to 2-2. McLoughlin has allowed only one earned run over his last 12 appearances and has now recorded six consecutive scoreless outings.

St. Lucie added three more runs in the third inning when Snyder launched his second home run of the season. The three-run shot brought home Mike Tauchman and Guzman and extended the Mets' advantage to 6-0.

Snyder continued his strong afternoon with a triple in the seventh inning. Branny De Oleo then hit his seventh home run of the season, a two-run shot that pushed St. Lucie's lead to 8-1.

Palm Beach made the game interesting in the bottom of the seventh.

Yairo Padilla hit his first home run of the season, a grand slam against Ernesto Mercedes, as the Cardinals scored five runs in the inning and cut the Mets' lead to 8-6.

Palm Beach brought the potential tying run to the plate in the ninth after Trevor Haskins was hit by a pitch. Miguel Mejias responded by striking out the next three batters to finish the game and earn his third save of the season.

St. Lucie pitchers combined for 17 strikeouts, marking the third consecutive game in which the Mets recorded double-digit strikeouts.

The Mets improved to 8-14 in the second half and 41-47 overall. Palm Beach fell to 13-10 in the second half and 65-43 overall.

St. Lucie will have an off day Monday before opening a new series against the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels on Tuesday. First pitch is scheduled for 6:05 p.m.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Fire District terminates 3 firefighters, suspends 2 others after hazing investigation
cards.teaser: Three firefighters were terminated and two others suspended following an investigation into allegations that senior firefighters used a modified bug zapper to administer electric shocks to probationary firefighters.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County Fire District on Saturday released investigative reports detailing allegations of hazing and workplace misconduct that led to the termination of 3 firefighters and the suspension of 2 others. According to the district, administrators first received videos in March 2026 showing what they described as senior firefighters using a modified bug zapper to administer electric shocks to probationary and apprentice firefighters while on duty. The district said the incidents occurred during shifts in March and September 2024. The videos prompted Fire Chief Jeff Lee to hire an outside attorney to conduct an independent investigation rather than handle the matter internally.

Attorney J.K. Keller, of Allen, Norton & Blue, concluded that a preponderance of the evidence showed probationary employees had been subjected to hazing by senior firefighters and supervisors. Keller also determined the conduct violated multiple district policies, including workplace violence and employee conduct rules. The district said it followed Keller's recommendations by terminating 3 employees and issuing 48-hour unpaid suspensions to 2 others. The investigative report describes videos showing probationary firefighters being questioned while connected to the modified device and receiving electrical shocks when they answered incorrectly. Other videos allegedly show probationary firefighters voluntarily allowing themselves to be shocked while coworkers looked on. Investigators concluded that any claimed consent was undermined by the power imbalance between senior firefighters and probationary employees. The disciplined employees have exercised their contractual rights to challenge the actions through the grievance and arbitration process.

cards.headline: Safe Kids Treasure Coast offering free pool alarms to Martin County residents
cards.teaser: The Florida Department of Health and Safe Kids Treasure Coast are providing a limited supply of free pool alarms to qualifying Martin County residents with residential pools.
cards.body:
The Florida Department of Health and Safe Kids Treasure Coast are providing a limited supply of free pool alarms to qualifying Martin County residents with residential pools.

According to the coalition, a pool alarm serves as one layer of protection and should always be used alongside close adult supervision, pool barriers and water safety education to help prevent drowning. The program emphasizes that pool alarms are not a standalone safety solution but rather part of a comprehensive approach to water safety. Residents should note that a 9-volt battery is required to operate the alarm, but the battery is not included with the free alarm.

The program offers one alarm per household to Martin County residents who have a residential pool. There are no income or priority group requirements for the program, making it available to any qualifying resident regardless of financial status. Safe Kids Treasure Coast is asking residents to fill out an online survey to determine their eligibility for the program. The alarms are available while supplies last, so residents interested in obtaining one should act promptly.

For more information about the free pool alarm program, residents can call (772) 462-3501. The initiative aims to increase water safety awareness and provide practical tools to help prevent drowning incidents in residential pools throughout Martin County. By distributing these alarms at no cost, the program seeks to remove financial barriers that might otherwise prevent families from implementing additional safety measures around their pools.

cards.headline: JetBlue cancels Vero Beach to JFK route in September due to low demand
cards.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast.

Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates. "It's just the way that that market works, and air carriers will fluctuate based off of demand," Dambeck said. He explained that JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route. "Just wasn't seeing what they were hoping for," Dambeck said. Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. Ahern emphasized the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach. "It's easy. It's close," Ahern said.

While the JFK route is ending, Dambeck said the Boston route is performing well. "Boston is seeing great demand," Dambeck said. Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time. As for whether the JFK route could return in the future, Dambeck said the door is not closed. "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back," Dambeck said.

All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds. JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information.

cards.headline: Flip City Gym and Cheer gymnasts earn top 15 national finish, qualify for Junior Olympics
cards.teaser: Three gymnasts from Flip City Gym and Cheer secured a top 15 finish at AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee last month and qualified for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month. Sk
cards.body:
Three gymnasts from Flip City Gym and Cheer secured a top 15 finish at AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee last month and qualified for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month. Skylar Rose-Daris, Victoria Supan, and Charli Rine represented the gym at the national competition and will advance to compete at the higher level. The trio each discovered gymnastics through unique experiences, with Rose-Daris crediting her ability to do a cartwheel, Supan finding inspiration from watching gymnasts on YouTube, and Rine enjoying the opportunity to continuously learn new skills.

Head Coach Candice Lazuka praised the team's performance throughout the season, noting they competed at local meets before advancing through states and regionals to reach nationals. At the AAU Nationals competition in Knoxville, the team delivered an exceptional performance that nearly achieved a perfect score. Lazuka explained that earning a perfect 10 is extremely difficult, but the gymnasts managed to score a 9.9, coming very close to perfection. The strong showing at nationals secured their qualification for the Junior Olympics.

The three gymnasts expressed excitement about the upcoming opportunity to compete at the Junior Olympics in Iowa. Rose-Daris said it's going to be really fun that she's going to an entire different part of the world. Supan described her feelings about the achievement, saying it's happy and exciting at the same time. The young athletes are preparing to take on competitors from across the country at the prestigious event.

Looking ahead to the Junior Olympics competition, the gymnasts are setting their goals and focusing on specific events. When asked what she is focused on heading into the Junior Olympics, Rine said getting first place on floors. The qualification represents a significant achievement for both the individual gymnasts and Flip City Gym and Cheer as a whole. The team's progression from local competitions through the state and regional levels to nationals, and now to the Junior Olympics, demonstrates the dedication and skill development that Lazuka has cultivated in her athletes. The upcoming competition in Iowa will provide Rose-Daris, Supan, and Rine the chance to test themselves against the nation's top junior gymnasts.

cards.headline: Boca Raton TLC Program Offers Summer Service Projects for South Florida Families
cards.teaser: B'nai Torah Congregation's TLC Program connects volunteers with hands-on service projects ranging from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking and literacy efforts.
cards.body:
B'nai Torah Congregation's TLC Program is offering South Florida families a range of hands-on service projects this summer, from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking, literacy efforts and care for seniors. The program, led by Summer Faerman, connects volunteers of all ages with mitzvah opportunities, or meaningful good deeds, as part of the congregation's broader community outreach efforts.

The TLC Program stands for Tzedakah, Learning and Chesed, and has made service a central part of synagogue life since 2012. The program provides a way for individuals and families to put Jewish values into action while helping people in need across South Florida. It addresses multiple community concerns including hunger, homelessness, literacy, elder care, vulnerable populations and special needs. Organizers emphasize that the projects are open to everyone in the community, not only members of B'nai Torah Congregation, with the goal of making service practical, welcoming and easy to begin.

Participants can volunteer in various ways throughout the summer. Projects include making sandwiches, serving meals, collecting and cleaning shoes, stocking Little Free Pantries, preparing backpacks for back-to-school efforts, creating Bags of Hope and helping seniors with technology. Organizers plan to demonstrate volunteer projects such as wrapping presents, making flower arrangements, preparing sandwiches, collecting shoes and assembling supplies for people in need. The variety of options allows families to choose activities that match their interests and schedules.

As summer continues, the TLC Program offers families a way to stay connected, teach children about giving back and support neighbors throughout South Florida. B'nai Torah Congregation says the program is built around the idea that small acts of service can strengthen the larger community. More information about the TLC Program is available through B'nai Torah Congregation's website.

hero.headline: Byron Donalds, David Jolly Lead Florida Governor's Race as Primary Nears
hero.teaser: Republican U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds and Democrat David Jolly hold commanding positions in Florida's governor's race with the August 18 primary approaching. A Tyson Group survey rele
hero.body:
Republican U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds and Democrat David Jolly hold commanding positions in Florida's governor's race with the August 18 primary approaching. A Tyson Group survey released this week placed Donalds at 48% among Republicans, followed by Lt. Gov. Jay Collins at 9%, businessman James Fishback at 8%, and former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner at 4%. About 26% of respondents remained undecided. Donalds has raised more than $90 million across his campaign operation and received President Donald Trump's endorsement.

The Republican primary has grown increasingly contentious as Collins, who was appointed lieutenant governor by Gov. Ron DeSantis in August 2025, attempts to consolidate support despite not receiving DeSantis's endorsement. During a Thursday campaign call, Collins positioned himself as the strongest alternative to Donalds and urged Renner to leave the race, saying the primary is between Donalds and himself. Meanwhile, Fishback faces challenges on multiple fronts. The Front Line, a Republican group aligned with U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz, announced a $400,000 campaign targeting Fishback over statements the group characterizes as antisemitic. The artificial intelligence-generated ad depicts Fishback as a talking fish making racist comments.

Collins is also challenging whether Fishback meets Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governors. A two-day hearing on the residency question is scheduled to begin July 21 in Tallahassee. The residency challenge adds another complication to Fishback's campaign as he attempts to gain traction in a race where Donalds maintains a significant polling advantage over the rest of the Republican field.

On the Democratic side, Jolly moved this week to address his past business and political relationship with Clearwater financier Leo Govoni. Federal prosecutors allege Govoni and accountant John Witeck stole more than $100 million from a nonprofit managing trust funds for people with disabilities, with the alleged scheme operating from 2009 through 2025. Jolly previously worked as a vice president at Boston Finance Group, a Govoni-controlled company, and Govoni served as a finance co-chairman during Jolly's unsuccessful 2016 U.S. Senate campaign. Jolly is not a defendant in the case. The connection nonetheless presents a challenge for Jolly as he seeks to maintain his lead in the Democratic primary while managing questions about his past associations with individuals now facing serious federal charges.

hero.headline: Two Martin County brush fires contained, more expected this summer
hero.teaser: Martin County saw two brush fires this week, including one sparked by a lightning strike, both now fully contained and being monitored by the Florida Forest Service.
hero.body:
Two brush fires broke out in Martin County this week, including one ignited by a lightning strike, and both are now fully contained and under monitoring by the Florida Forest Service. Officials warn that the conditions causing these fires will continue throughout the summer months as peak fire season persists in the region.

David Grubitch, a mitigation specialist and spokesperson with the Florida Forest Service, said summertime heat is drying out fine dead fuels, making them highly receptive when lightning strikes occur. However, he emphasized that residents should not be alarmed by these conditions, as they are typical for this time of year. Grubitch explained that while rain often extinguishes fires immediately after they start, some fires can travel underground and resurface days later, making them more difficult to detect and contain.

The Florida Forest Service is relying on public assistance to help monitor and respond to brush fires quickly. Grubitch stressed that residents play a crucial role in helping the department do its job effectively and urged people to never assume someone else has already reported a brush fire they spot. He emphasized the importance of immediate notification, saying that if residents see something, they should say something, as it can make all the difference in how quickly crews are able to get a fire under control. Quick reporting remains one of the most effective tools in preventing small fires from becoming larger, more dangerous blazes that threaten homes and natural areas.

With summer conditions expected to continue creating favorable environments for brush fires, the Florida Forest Service will maintain its heightened monitoring and response efforts throughout the season. The department continues to track contained fires and remains prepared to respond to new incidents as they arise. Residents are encouraged to remain vigilant and report any signs of smoke or fire to local authorities immediately, regardless of whether they believe others may have already called it in. Officials stress that multiple reports of the same fire are preferable to a fire going unreported and potentially spreading out of control.

cards.headline: Unity in the Community event connects Fort Pierce families with services and public safety demonstrations
cards.teaser: The annual Fort Pierce event brought together families with community services and public safety demonstrations.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce hosted its annual Unity in the Community event, connecting families with services, public safety demonstrations and community resources. The event builds bridges between police and residents in the city.

The gathering provided opportunities for Fort Pierce families to access community resources and interact with local public safety agencies. The event focused on strengthening relationships between law enforcement and the residents they serve.

hero.headline: Indian River County families can apply for free or reduced-price student meals starting July 15
hero.teaser: Families in Indian River County are able to apply for free or reduced price meals for students starting July 15.
hero.body:
Families in Indian River County can apply for free or reduced-price meals for students starting July 15 through the district's online portal. While six schools in the county will automatically provide free meals to all students during the 2026-2027 school year through federal nutrition programs, other families may still qualify based on household size and income levels.

District officials are encouraging families to submit one application per household to determine eligibility. The application process begins at www.LINQConnect.com, where parents must either sign in to an existing account or create a new one. After logging in, families should search for Indian River County Public Schools in Vero Beach and add their student to the application using the Student ID number and the child's formal name as it appears in FOCUS, the district's student information system. The application can be accessed from the website homepage by clicking School Services at the top menu and then selecting Free and Reduced Meal Application.

The application requires families to provide information about household size and income to determine eligibility for the federal nutrition programs. By submitting a single application for all children in the household, families can streamline the process and find out if they qualify for free meals, reduced-price meals, or neither option. The program is designed to ensure that students have access to nutritious meals during the school day regardless of their family's financial situation.

Families who have questions about the meal programs or need assistance with the application process can contact Shawn O'Keefe, the district's nutrition services director. O'Keefe can be reached by phone at (772) 564-5041 or by email at shawn.okeefe@indianriverschools.org. District officials recommend that families apply as early as possible to ensure their eligibility status is determined before the start of the 2026-2027 school year.
